name: su
description: Switches to another user account in the current shell (substitute user).

flags.description: Become root (prompts for the ROOT password, not yours).
Switch to another user (prompts for that user's password).
-l: full login shell — resets environment and home directory. Always prefer su - over plain su for root.
Run a single command as the target user, then exit.

examples.explanation: Becomes root with a full login environment. The prompt changes to #, and $PATH now includes /sbin and /usr/sbin.
Runs a single command as alice without an interactive session.
Becomes the postgres service user with its proper environment — the standard way to reach database administrative shells.

about: su authenticates with the TARGET user's password, while sudo authenticates with YOUR password against the sudoers policy. On distributions where the root account has no password set (Ubuntu by default), su - cannot work and sudo is the only path.
useCases: Switch to service accounts (postgres, www-data) that have no sudo policy.
Become root on systems where root has a password.
mistakes: Using plain su instead of su - and getting "command not found" for admin tools — the PATH lacks /usr/sbin.
Confusing su and sudo password expectations.
warnings: A root su shell bypasses sudoers logging granularity; on audited systems prefer sudo for per-command logging.
